issues.legal_issue: A court must record a compromise in pending litigation when it is satisfied that the compromise is genuine and lawful.
material_facts: The parties signed and accepted a compromise covering the entire subject matter of the litigation.
The compromise stated that each son had received payment in exchange for relinquishing his interest.
One son later disputed receiving the stipulated payment and opposed recording the compromise.
The Court found the compromise genuine and lawful.
issues.conclusion: The compromise had to be accepted and recorded, and the suit disposed of in accordance with its terms.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution and Order 23, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, once the Court is satisfied that a compromise is genuine and lawful, it must record it. The Court approved the principle in Bhoja Govinda Maikap & Anr. v. Janaki Dei & Ors., AIR (1980) Orissa 108.

predicates.compromise_recording_proceeding: A party asks a court to record a compromise in pending litigation.
predicates.compromise_signed_and_accepted: The parties signed the compromise and accepted its terms.
predicates.court_satisfied_genuine_and_lawful: The court found that the compromise was genuine and lawful.

issues.definition: When a court is asked to record a compromise in pending litigation, the parties signed and accepted it, and the court finds it genuine and lawful, the court must record it.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer made after a binding compromise has extinguished the transferor’s interest creates no interest in the property for the transferee.
material_facts: The compromise provided for a son to relinquish his interest in the disputed property in exchange for payment, and the signed document stated that the payment had been received.
The Court accepted the compromise as genuine and binding.
The Court found that the challenged sales occurred after the compromise and found no acceptable evidence of prior agreements for sale.
The sales concerned property in pending litigation, and the transferees were in possession under the sale deeds.
issues.conclusion: The sale deeds were invalid, the transferees acquired no interest in the property, and their possession was without authority of law; they were directed to deliver vacant possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and held that the transferees acquired no right where the transferor had no interest left to convey after the binding compromise. The judgment’s headnote also states that a sale of suit property pendente lite by a party, before compromise, is not valid; the Court’s factual finding in this case was that the challenged sales followed the compromise.

predicates.pending_property_litigation: The property was the subject of pending litigation when the transfer occurred.
predicates.binding_compromise_extinguished_transfer: A binding compromise had extinguished the transferor’s interest in the property.
predicates.transfer_occurred_after_compromise: The transfer occurred after the compromise had extinguished the transferor’s interest.

issues.definition: If property in pending litigation is transferred after a binding compromise has extinguished the transferor’s interest, the transferee acquires no property interest.
